title: Holidays in Prostokvashino
author: Eduard Uspensky
short_summary: A resourceful boy named Uncle Fyodor (nicknamed for how grown-up he acts) leaves the city with a talking cat named Matroskin to live in a quiet countryside house in the village of Prostokvashino. Together with a shy dog named Sharik, they build a happy, unusual little household — solving problems his own way, since he acts far more sensibly than most grown-ups.
extended_summary:
A resourceful boy named Uncle Fyodor (nicknamed for how grown-up he acts) leaves the city with a talking cat named Matroskin to live in a quiet countryside house in the village of Prostokvashino. Together with a shy dog named Sharik, they build a happy, unusual little household — solving problems his own way, since he acts far more sensibly than most grown-ups.

As the trio settles in, they raise a cow, deal with a mischievous local postman, and slowly turn their ramshackle house into a real home. Meanwhile, Uncle Fyodor's worried parents search for him back in the city, not realizing their son is doing just fine — better, in some ways, than when he was under their constant watch.

questions.prompt: Who does Uncle Fyodor move to the countryside with?
questions.explanation: Uncle Fyodor moves with Matroskin, a cat who can talk.
Matroskin is the clever, practical cat who moves to Prostokvashino with Uncle Fyodor.

questions.prompt: Sort each character into the right group.
questions.explanation: The new countryside household is made up of Uncle Fyodor, Matroskin, and Sharik, while his parents stay behind, searching for him.

questions.prompt: Why do you think Uncle Fyodor manages so well on his own?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the story suggests he's simply more responsible and calm than most children his age.
